what: Webcam Test checks that your camera works before a video call, interview or online exam. It shows the live picture and tells you which camera is used, the resolution you really get and the frame rate measured from the video.

You can switch between cameras, ask for a higher resolution, flip the mirror view and take a snapshot to save as a PNG picture. Clear messages explain what to do if the camera is blocked, busy or missing.
The video stays on your device. Nothing is recorded or uploaded.
uses: Check your picture, light and framing before Zoom, Teams, Google Meet or Skype.
Find out whether the problem is the camera, the browser permission or another app using it.
See the real resolution and frame rate it delivers, such as 1080p at 30 frames a second.
Switch between a laptop camera and a USB webcam to see which looks better.
Grab a snapshot and download it as a PNG file.
tutorial: Your browser asks for permission. Click Allow.
The live video appears. Move around and check the light and focus.
After permission is given, the Camera menu lists all cameras. "Ask for resolution" and "Ask for frame rate" request other settings.
The boxes show the camera name, the resolution and frame rate you actually get, the camera's maximum and how many cameras were found.
Press "Take snapshot". A small picture appears; click it to download the PNG.
Press Stop when you are finished so the camera light turns off.
features: See your camera picture straight away.
Measured from the video itself, not just what the camera claims.
Switch between built-in, USB and virtual cameras.
Show the picture flipped like a mirror, or as others see you.
Check the picture large on your screen.
Clear steps for blocked, busy or missing cameras.

example.title: Worked example: checking a camera before an interview
example.text: Sam has a job interview on Teams in ten minutes. He opens Webcam Test and presses Start camera, then Allow. The picture is dark, so he turns on a lamp. The boxes show "HD Webcam", 1280 × 720 and 30.0 fps. He takes a snapshot to check how he looks, then presses Stop and joins the call.

tips: If the picture is black, close other apps that use the camera, such as Zoom, Teams or the Camera app.
Some laptops have a camera switch, a sliding cover or a key (often F8 or F10) that turns the camera off.
Light from in front of you looks much better than a window behind you.
A low frame rate often means poor light; cameras slow down to collect more light.
On a phone, use the Camera menu to switch between the front and back camera.
problems: Click the camera or lock icon next to the web address, allow the camera and press Start camera again. On a phone, also check the browser's camera permission in the phone settings.
Plug in the webcam, check its cable and switch, and make sure it is enabled in your computer's settings.
Another app or tab is using the camera. Close it and try again.
The resolution is lower than expected
Choose a higher setting in "Ask for resolution". Some cameras give their best resolution only at a lower frame rate, or only over a USB 3 port.
